settings.title: Flat-Fee Nil T2 Filing for Dormant Construction Corporations

settings.editor:
A trades corporation between phases still owes a return each year, with tools and a trailer that may still be owned, a workers compensation account still open, and the entity sitting on the registry waiting for the next job. We file those seasons at $300.00 plus HST per tax year so the company stays ready to bid.

Whether you took a payroll job with a larger builder, split a partnership and stopped bidding, sold the trailer, or are between contracts, we test the season against released holdback, subcontractor payments and equipment disposals, then prepare and transmit the return. An unbroken filing history is what bonding and prequalification ask for later.

settings.title: What an Unfiled Season Costs a Dormant Construction Corporation

settings.description_text: No work does not mean no return. The year is outstanding until it is filed.
The Agency can require the season be filed, on a timetable that it sets rather than you.
Sureties and general contractors want filing history before they take a trade on.
Dissolution needs every season filed first, so the entity cannot be abandoned.

settings.editor:
A dormant trades corporation is almost always kept on purpose, because the next job might need it. What makes it usable is the record behind it, and a gap is what damages the record.

Each empty season is $300.00 plus HST per tax year. Filing them in order keeps the capital cost allowance on the trucks and tools carrying forward, and leaves the company ready to bid.

settings.html:
The year is nil

  • No contract, progress draw or change order was invoiced
  • No holdback from any earlier project was released to the corporation
  • No subcontractor, labourer or supplier was paid by it
  • No truck, machine, trailer or tool was sold, traded or scrapped
  • No warranty or deficiency claim was settled either way

The year is not nil

  • A statutory holdback was released, however old the project
  • Any subcontractor payment was made, which also brings a T5018
  • Equipment or a vehicle was sold, traded in or written off
  • A progress draw or final invoice went out on an old job
  • A deficiency or warranty settlement moved money

Due either way

  • A T2 for every tax year until the corporation is dissolved
  • A T183CORP signed by an authorised signing officer, per tax year
  • The GST/HST account, which expects returns until it is closed
  • The workers compensation account, closed with the provincial board
  • Schedule 8, for as long as any equipment is still owned

Dormant construction corporations are filed the same way wherever the registered office sits, because the return is prepared and transmitted electronically from end to end. There is nothing to print, nothing to post and nothing to sign in person.

Where the corporation was incorporated changes the registry, not the return. An Ontario corporation answers to the Ontario Business Registry, and corporations in British Columbia, Alberta, Quebec and Saskatchewan each answer to their own. The T2 itself is federal and identical in all of them. Within Ontario, a corporation registered in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton or Ottawa is filed on the same terms and at the same price as one anywhere else in the country.

Two provinces add a return the federal T2 does not cover. A Quebec corporation also files the CO-17 and an Alberta corporation also files the AT1. Both are separate provincial returns, and neither is included in the $300.00 plus HST fee.

settings.title: Nil T2 Filing FAQs for Dormant Construction Corporations

items.item_title: I took a payroll job and parked the company. Does it still file?
A holdback from an old job was finally released. Is that year nil?
I sold the truck and the trailer. What does that do?
I paid one subcontractor for a small favour. Does that matter?
Does my workers compensation account close with the T2?
What about the GST/HST number on a dormant company?
There is still a shareholder loan on the books. Is the year nil?
My partner and I each own half. Who signs?
Can I keep the company dormant and bid again in a few years?
How far back can unfiled seasons be filed?

settings.editor: Yes, every year it exists. Your T4 income is personal. The corporation owes its own T2 until dissolution, and a season with no contracts in it is nil.
No. Released holdback is contract revenue in the year of receipt, whatever year the work was done, which makes that one an ordinary return.
It is a disposal. Against the depreciated value it produces either a recapture or a terminal loss, the year stops being nil, and the figures belong on Schedule 8.
Twice over. The payment is activity, so the year is not nil, and it also brings a T5018 contract payment information return of its own.
No. A provincial board account keeps expecting its own reporting until you close it with the board. The corporate return has no effect on it.
That account is separate and keeps expecting returns until it is closed on Form RC145. A dormant corporation with an open number still has obligations of its own.
Usually yes. A loan balance that neither grew nor shrank is a balance sheet figure on Schedule 100, not activity. An advance or a repayment during the year is.
One authorised signing officer signs per tax year. Both of you still appear on Schedule 50 at 50% each.
Yes, and that is the usual reason to file rather than dissolve. An unbroken filing history is what keeps the entity usable for bonding and prequalification later.
As far back as they go. Each is its own T2 at $300.00 plus HST per tax year with its own T183CORP, transmitted earliest first so equipment balances reconcile.
